title: Copy a plan without sharing its containers

blocks.text: Riverbend Water (invented for this practice) plans its main-replacement program with `Plan` records. Besides a yearly budget, a plan holds, for each district, a list with the number of crews available in each month, and a list of tags. Analysts copy a plan to try a storm-reserve variant, then change budgets and individual months in the copy.

Write `copy_plan(p, plan_id, name, by)` in `plan.py`. It returns a new `Plan` with the given id, name and author, inputs equal to `p`'s, and `parent_id` naming `p`. Nothing the copy holds may be an object that `p` also holds, at any depth, so that no edit to the copy, however deep, can change `p`. About four lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass
class Plan:
    plan_id: str
    name: str
    budget: dict[int, int]                     # year -> $k
    crews: dict[str, list[int]]                # district -> crews available in each month
    parent_id: str | None = None
    created_by: str = ""
    tags: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)


def copy_plan(p: Plan, plan_id: str, name: str, by: str) -> Plan:
    """A new plan with p's inputs, no container shared with p, and a link back to p."""
    return Plan(plan_id, name, budget=dict(p.budget),
                crews={district: list(months) for district, months in p.crews.items()},
                parent_id=p.plan_id, created_by=by, tags=list(p.tags))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    base = Plan("R-1", "base", {2027: 900}, {"north": [3, 3, 4]}, created_by="analyst-a")
    print(copy_plan(base, "R-2", "storm reserve", "analyst-b"))

cases.says: the copy carries the new id, name and author, and inputs equal to the parent's
changing a budget year on the copy leaves the parent's budget unchanged
changing one month's crews on the copy leaves the parent's month list unchanged
the copy's parent is the plan it was copied from, not that plan's own parent

origin.section: A Copy Shares Nothing Mutable With Its Parent

concepts: a copy gets its own containers at every depth and a link to its parent
